title: 2023 AMC 10A Problem 19
statement: The line segment formed by \(A(1, 2)\) and \(B(3, 3)\) is rotated to the line segment formed by \(A'(3, 1)\) and \(B'(4, 3)\) about the point \(P(r, s).\) What is \(|r - s|?\)

solutions.text: A rotation keeps its center equidistant from each point and its image. So \(P\) is equidistant from \(A\) and \(A',\) and from \(B\) and \(B',\) which puts it at the intersection of two perpendicular bisectors. The bisector of \(BB'\) from \((3,3)\) to \((4,3)\) is \(x = 3.5.\) The bisector of \(AA'\) from \((1,2)\) to \((3,1)\) is \(2x - y = 2.5.\) Then \(y = 2(3.5) - 2.5 = 4.5,\) so \(P = (3.5, 4.5)\) and \(|r - s| = |3.5 - 4.5| = 1.\) Thus, E is the correct answer.
hints: The rotation center is equidistant from each point and its image, so it lies on the perpendicular bisectors of \(AA'\) and \(BB'\)
Intersect the perpendicular bisector of \(BB'\) (a vertical line) with that of \(AA'\)
